badSpecialNumber.description: An object that has a $number member and is not exactly one of the four named numbers.

builder.description: The name of a function of the package that builds a tree.

messageIncludes.description: Fragments the failure's message contains, each after the end of the one before.
Fragments the failure's message contains, each after the end of the one before.

function.description: The name of a built-in function of the package.

stderrIncludes.description: Fragments standard error contains, each after the end of the one before.

stderrStartsWith.description: The text standard error begins with.

stdoutStartsWith.description: The text standard output begins with.

files.description: File name to file text. Contents are text, so a number such as 1e999 reaches the parser as written.

computedValue.description: A ComputedValue as the trilean package represents it; validated by the runner of the package that owns it.

context.description: A context to match, or * for any context.

expectIssuePaths.description: Paths each of which at least one issue of a rejected document names: an issue is `<path>: <text>`, and the text is a schema library's, not the implementation's to pin.

expectSubset.description: For a rejected document whose issues hold a third-party library's text, which the implementation does not own: the outcome without the issue text, with `expectIssuePaths` for the paths. It names at least one key; an object matches when every key it gives matches, an array matches element by element at the same length, any other value must be equal.

value.description: The value the evaluation settles on; a case always states it.

ignoreCase.description: Compare message and messageIncludes without regard to letter case, as an original written as a case-insensitive pattern did.

messageIncludes.description: Fragments the reason's message contains, each after the end of the one before.

message.description: A fragment of the message the evaluation threw.

expectCalls.description: The resolver calls in the order they were made.

from.description: The original test title this case came from, as `<test file>: <title>`, or `recorded: <package> <source file> (<what>)` for a behaviour recorded from the implementation because no test covered it. The prefix tells a pinned original from a recorded behaviour.

id.description: Unique across the whole corpus. Lower-case ASCII letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores, so every loader orders ids the same way.

json.description: Any JSON value. An object with a $number member is the number it names and has no other member; a $number member holding anything but one of the four names is refused.

nonEmptyText.description: A text that holds at least one code unit.

reason.description: Why one side cannot run the case. Required with skip, and only with skip.

dialect.description: The language the pattern is in: trilean, the default, or ecmascript, for a pattern an unflagged ECMAScript RegExp reads, with each result recorded from it.

regexNode.description: A trilean-regex abstract syntax node, with the field names of the package's ast module. An unbounded repeat omits max.

ranges.description: The positive set; never empty, since a class holds at least one item. Each range's from is not above its to, which the schema cannot express and every loader checks.

oneOf.description: max is omitted for an unbounded repeat. min is not above max, which the schema cannot express and every loader checks.

regexNodeSubset.description: A partial regexNode for astSubset: an object that matches when every key it gives matches (an array matches element by element at the same length, any other value when equal). It names at least one key, since an empty subset matches every tree.

error.description: What the refusal is pinned to: its index, fragments of its reason, or both. At least one, since an empty error is satisfied by any refusal for any reason.

index.description: Offset in UTF-16 code units into pattern. Given only where the case pins it.

message.description: Fragments the reason text of the refusal contains, each after the end of the one before. The reason is the part of the error that says why the pattern was refused: not the index, the echoed pattern or the position marker. Given only where the original test asserted a message, or where the case is recorded.

resolution.description: What one resolver call returns: a value, an absence (known, or not yet known), or an exception the resolver throws with that message.

expect.description: The exact text the value serialises to.

input.description: JSON text, whose order of members is the order the text gives.

schema.description: The export name of a tree or value schema of the package.

skip.description: Names the implementation that skips the case, for a case one implementation cannot run: ts for a case the TypeScript implementation skips, rust for a case every build of the Rust implementation skips, wherever it runs (native, or wasm under Node, a browser or Workers). Always with a reason.

specialNumber.description: A number the canonical JSON form cannot hold, written as an object: a negative zero (a canonical form writes it as 0), an infinity or NaN.

text.description: A string as a sequence of UTF-16 code units, which is what the TypeScript implementation and the patterns' index counts are in. A JSON string, which must be well-formed Unicode so every loader can read it, or an object holding the code units themselves for content a JSON string cannot carry, an unpaired surrogate.

tolerance.description: How far a number may be from the one a case gives. Numbers compare exactly unless a case gives a tolerance: `ulps`, the number of representable doubles between the two numbers, or `absolute`, a distance the two numbers must be strictly closer than. A tolerance holds for every number in the value that is compared, treats both zeros as one value, and never applies to an expectation that is not finite.

schema.description: The export name of a schema of the package.

description: One corpus file: an object holding a non-empty list of cases. Every case names the behaviour it pins with a unique id and a from, and takes a kind-specific shape. See README.md for the rules a schema cannot express.
